To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pancreas in infants has a variable anatomy in relation to the SMV and that a 75% pancreatectomy as determined by the SMV will resect a mean of only about 53.5%.

1. the uncinate process is a major part of the pancreas and should be included in all subtotal pancreatectomys, 2. the uncinate is a variable proportion of the pancreas in relation to the SMV, and 3. a subtotal pancreatecotomy based on the SMV is likely to result in a resection of less pancreatic tissue than expected.

1) the uncinate process is an integral part of the pancreas and should not be considered an isolated entity; 2) the uncinate is not a fixed anatomical entity; 3) the pancreatic tail is not a fixed entity; 4) the pancreatic tail and the uncinate can be on either side of the superior mesentric artery and vein (SMV); 5) the uncinate can weigh up to 56.6% of the total pancreas weight;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of surgical anatomy in the performance of pancreatectomy in children.
the surgical anatomy of children's pancreas and the importance of this knowledge to pancreatectomized patients with nesidiobastosis.
the surgical anatomy of pancreatic resections in children and the importance of this information in performing pancreatectomises.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SMV does not serve as a landmark for a "subtotal" 75% resective procedure in the pediatric patient.
a subtotal pancreasectomy should include at least 75% of the gland, and this can be done without the use of the SMV as a landmark.
the uncinate process is an integral part of the head of the pancreatic gland and should never be resected in a pancreatectomy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a subtotal pan createctomy should not include tissue to the left of SMV, but should include the uncinate process.
the SMV should never be used as a landmark for pancreatectomization.
a "subtotal" pan createctomy should be based upon the anatomy of the individual child and should not be performed based upon presumed landmarks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncinate process of the pancreas is a major component of the pancreas and should be included in any subtotal pancreatectomys.
the uncinate process of the pancreas is a significant component of the pancreatic mass and must be removed to perform a true subtotal resection.
